original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: The equality case of the six-source depth-two connector at characteristic 7: a length-42 floor word in which every weight-3 mask is realized only on the pairs with s+t in {3,45}. That forces all 19 pairs (s,45-s) for s=4..22 to be weight-3 realizations. This package proves no such word exists. The unrestricted c=7 existence question stays open.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the unsigned dirty connector alphabet fixed and answers a released obstruction question: Nick Petalas's 2026-11-03 handoff on open question 1 of JosieElliston's PR6141, the tight diagonal model at c=7. A new operation is not the missing step; the equality case of the existing depth-two schedule is.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the recursive-interface schedule. It does not change a supplier, a consumer, or kappa. Ruling out the 20-slot diagonal cover removes the only equality case in which weight-3 masks meet C(6,3) with no spare pair.
stop_rule: Stop once the diagonal equality case is proved empty, or stop if the centre classification admits a weight-3 sum with no coordinate equal to 14.
evidence: Written proof plus an exhaustive standard-library check of every length-22 centre count: 300 weight-3 centre realizations, 180 of type (0,1) and 120 of type (3,1), with 480 coordinates equal to 14. The one-step recurrence leaves 14 fixed, so that coordinate is 7 in q_4, which is impossible. Four negative controls reject a near-miss centre, a move of 14, an all-lambda-one centre, and a length-4 prefix that already contains a 7.

open_questions.question: Does a six-source depth-two block exist at c=7 if weight-3 masks may use pairs off s+t=45?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The diagonal equality case is empty, so this is now the whole of PR6141 question 1 and the smallest open characteristic for a six-source depth-two block.
open_questions.first_step: Allow one diagonal index s in 4..22 to fail the weight-3 test and ask whether one off-diagonal pair can replace that mask without losing another.
open_questions.blocked_by: The lambda-invariance argument uses every diagonal index. A single skipped index breaks the induction, and no replacement inequality is proved here.

open_questions.question: Can the same frozen-14 obstruction be adapted to a human proof of the c=5 and c=6 exclusions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those exclusions are still solver verdicts (PR6141). At c=5 and c=6 the middle diagonal already has fewer than 20 slots, so the equality case is a different count.
open_questions.first_step: Classify the centre of s+t=kc+3 for c=5 and c=6 and see whether a frozen coordinate still reaches a prefix shorter than 7.
open_questions.blocked_by: Fewer slots means a proof must also bound off-diagonal pairs, which this argument does not do.
